subject: Dual partner coverage — truce and account routing plan
messages:
From: Emily Park <epark@orbitalleap.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: "",

Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Account coverage overlap — West Coast ISV vs consultancy claims

Jonas,

Hope you’re well — Emily here from Orbital Leap. We ran a quick pipeline audit ahead of our Q2 motion and noticed a handful of accounts (see attached 'orbital_claims_map.pdf') where both Orbital Leap and Catalyst Systems are listed as active partners/contact owners in Redwood’s partner portal.

Two asks:
- Can you confirm how Redwood currently routes partner leads and attribution?
- We’d like a short call next week to align on account ownership so we don’t duplicate outreach into a couple of strategic target logos.

High-level examples in the attachment: Orion Analytics, PacificMed, and GreenGrid — both partners have running opportunities and there’s overlap on outreach cadence. Happy to share our POA if helpful.

Best,
Emily Park
Head of Partnerships
Orbital Leap
[Attachment: orbital_claims_map.pdf (pdf)]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Park <epark@orbitalleap.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Account coverage overlap — West Coast ISV vs consultancy claims

Emily — thanks for the note and the map. I’m copying Marissa and Karthik (partnerships + alliances) so we can triage.

Quick response: Redwood’s routing logic defaults to the first partner who registered the account/contact and then to the partner with the closest integration fit (ISV vs services). But we’ve seen inconsistencies when partners bulk-import CRM records, which looks like the case here.

I can set up a brief sync with both partners next week — Thu 11:00am PT or Fri 9:00am PT? Also, we’ll propose an interim routing table to avoid deal interference while we finalize the long-term rules.

—Jonas
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Account coverage overlap — West Coast ISV vs consultancy claims

Team — I pulled the portal exports and cross-referenced with partner-sourced lists. Attached is a proposed routing CSV (proposed_routing.csv) that tries to minimize conflict by applying a 3-tier rule:

1) Primary assignment: partner with existing paid deployment or active POC (within last 12 months)
2) Product-fit override: if the partner’s integration is a native ISV connector that reduces time-to-value by >50% (engineering check), prefer ISV for ingestion/platform accounts
3) Engagement cadence: if both parties show active sales motion (contact touches in last 30 days), create a co-sell pairing and designate a lead partner for commercial negotiations.

Applied to the three accounts Emily called out:
- Orion Analytics: assigned to Orbital Leap (active PoC, integration demo on file)
- PacificMed: co-sell (Catalyst has deeper compliance practice; Orbital Leap has platform integration)
- GreenGrid: assigned to Catalyst (services-led migration underway)

Notes / asks:
- We should surface a short 'partner claim' flag in the portal to prevent bulk overwrites.
- If legal is OK, propose a simple MOU for co-sell splits on co-owned deals (10/90 threshold example in doc).

I’ll be on the call Thursday 11:00am PT if that works for Emily and Catalyst.

-Marissa
VP, Alliances & GTM
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_routing.csv (csv)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Account coverage overlap — West Coast ISV vs consultancy claims

Marissa — this framework looks good. Two quick add-ons:
- For accounts where Catalyst is the SI lead, require an integration readiness note from the ISV (Orbital) before assigning product-owner rights. Prevents premature feature promises.
- For co-sell pairings, suggest an immediate temporary 'no outreach' window for 7 days while both partners align so the customer gets one coordinated cadence.

If both partners accept these constraints, legal can draft a 1-page handshake and I can route to finance for split approvals.

Karthik
Sr. Director, Partner Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Park <epark@orbitalleap.io>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@catalystsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood partner routing — agreed temporary mapping & handshake

Emily / Carlos — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from Redwood: 

1) Temporary routing map (effective immediately, see attached 'rdw_orbit_catalyst_handshake.docx'):
   - Orion Analytics -> Orbital Leap (primary)
   - PacificMed -> co-sell (Orbital Leap & Catalyst)
   - GreenGrid -> Catalyst Systems (primary)

2) Temporary rules we applied:
   - 7-day coordination window before any outbound sales sequence by either partner
   - Product-fit override: ISV must confirm integration readiness to own product-led deals
   - Finance will default to 70/30 revenue share on co-sell deals unless an alternative is negotiated in writing

3) Action items:
   - Emily: sign the one-page handshake (DocuSign link below) and upload minimal proof of active PoC for Orion Analytics.
   - Carlos: acknowledge co-sell on PacificMed and nominate the SI lead for diligence.
   - Marissa/Karthik: update portal flags and set the 7-day outreach hold.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/rdw/embedded/xyz-handshake-4821
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRDW-partner-maps

If we don’t see any objections by EOD Friday PT, this temporary map goes live. We’ll follow up with Legal to convert the one-pager into a recurring process template.

—Jonas
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rdw_orbit_catalyst_handshake.docx (docx)]
From: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@catalystsys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Park <epark@orbitalleap.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood partner routing — agreed temporary mapping & handshake

Jonas — appreciate the facilitation. Catalyst confirms co-sell on PacificMed and accepts the 7-day coordination window. I’ve added the SI lead (Ayesha Rao) to the shared drive for diligence. We’ll sign the handshake by EOD and share the migration plan.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendes
VP, Strategic Partnerships
Catalyst Systems
